sentence: This project studies genetic differences in healthy centenarians to find ways to develop drugs that target aging.
This project tries to predict which patients will have severe immune-related adverse events, using patient-reported outcomes and T-cell receptor sequencing.
This project builds tools that make it faster and simpler to measure proteoforms with mass spectrometry.
This project studies what drives high blood pressure at night in children with proteinuric glomerulopathies, looking at clinical predictors and molecular markers.
This project uses imaging of the human brain to see how fibrin deposition relates to progressive neurodegeneration over time.
This project builds methods to find natural selection in natural populations, including humans.
This project builds a way to quickly capture the 3D shape of single cells, including cell membranes and intracellular organelles.
This project offers analytical tools that find and measure toxicants and the body's responses to toxicant exposure.
This project studies how herpes simplex viruses enter human cells and how their viral proteins interact.
This project tests whether blocking a kinase protein that restrains T lymphocytes helps the body fight cancer and slows tumor growth.
This project maps the types of cells in the developing brains of humans, Rhesus macaque and marmoset using single nucleus RNA-sequencing.
This project uses Bayesian machine learning on brain development data from adolescents to study substance use risk and the effects of COVID-19.
This project tries to find and fix differences between population groups in who qualifies for medication therapy management services based on risk scores.
This project studies how lectin receptors control how long glycoproteins last in the blood and how this affects health and disease.
This project builds a genetics study of Alzheimer's disease in Asian Americans.
This project tests whether a strong dislike of ambiguity causes internalizing disorders such as depression and anxiety-related disorders, using computational modeling of decision-making.
This project tries to find and describe the proteins in Treponema pallidum, the syphilis bacterium, that interact with lipids and sterols.
This project builds fluorescent sensors that tell apart four classes of reactive aldehydes in living cells.
This project uses near-infrared optical imaging to find lung cancer tumors that are missed during surgery and bronchoscopy.
This project studies how a master gene regulator in the model organism responds to oleic acid to help the organism and extend lifespan.
